cues.title: The problem
cues.text: Someone on a live call needs what is true right now, not after it ends. This is Live, and the banner says plainly what it will not do.

cues.title: Play the sample conversation, and watch the brief evolve
cues.text: Press play. The brief is not redrawn from scratch on every line — the version number only moves forward when the server's own throttle decides a refresh is worth an LLM call. Watch it climb as the caller says more: a machine shop, binder jetting, a furnace, titanium and budget. Every claim is grounded, and the sources build up underneath.

cues.title: The transcript and the session's own numbers
cues.text: Next to the brief, the transcript and the session's own numbers: refreshes run, refreshes the throttle skipped, and how long the last one took.

cues.title: End the call, then find it again in Conversations
cues.text: Ending a session loses nothing — the brief, its sources and how it developed are kept. Conversations lists every call, and searching for something the caller actually said finds this one. Opening it shows the final brief, the full transcript, and every version the brief passed through, each timestamped and timed.

cues.title: Knowledge: what it is grounded in, a cited answer, and the pipeline behind it
cues.text: Knowledge shows what a prospect is grounded in — sample content here, honestly marked. The Ask tester runs the same pipeline a live turn does and shows its work: nine steps, timed. Ask something it knows and the answer carries a citation; ask something it does not and it hands off.

cues.title: The quality gate: the golden set, live
cues.text: Before a prospect is trusted to answer it clears this gate: the same ten questions, through the same pipeline, right now.

cues.title: Quality: the numbers, and a guard trip redacted
cues.text: Quality checks all of that in aggregate. And when someone tries an injection, the guard trips first — the log keeps the reason, never the text.

cues.title: Into the Operator panel
cues.text: Behind the product is an Operator panel for whoever runs the deployment, behind its own token. It sees the same session from the operator's side — every version the brief passed through, and how long each refresh took.

cues.title: Settings: read-only until it is unlocked
cues.text: Settings is a reading screen until this browser proves it is an operator. The same token unlocks it in place, on this page.

cues.title: Rebrand it while you watch
cues.text: Every setting this product reads from configuration is editable here. Type a partner's name into Branding: the preview repaints as you type, before anything is saved. Save, and the rail, the tab title and the action colour repaint underneath you — no reload, no restart. Reset the group and the environment's value comes straight back.

cues.title: The voice agent is configured from the product
cues.text: Everything voice runs on ElevenLabs, configured from in here rather than their dashboard. No key on this deployment, so the page says so. Add one and this panel shows where it and the live agent disagree.

cues.title: The API explorer: everything the workspace does, callable
cues.text: And everything you have watched the workspace do, an application can do. This explorer is built from the deployment's own OpenAPI document, so an operation cannot be added to the API and forgotten here. Find the voice turn, send it with the body already filled in, and the answer comes back with its citations and its timings — the same call the agent makes, written out as curl, ready to paste.
